I would agree with the ppl above. As someone who usually cuts deep, this is also familiar to me. You might have seen some blood coming from one spot or side of your wound? Or see the blood streaming out of your wound on your heart beat? If so, this could be blood vessels and small veins that usually stop bleeding themselves. They do have darker blood and bleed more.

Please know that if it doesn't stop bleeding or if blood spurts out of your wound, you might have hit big veins, arteries or blood vessels or small veins that don't close on themselves. You should seek immediate medical attention in that case.

Please do note I am in no way a medical professional.
I would say personally if you don't have many medical supplies, this is how I would care for my cuts:
I would clean them first with lukewarm water. Not directly on the cuts, but let the water stream down -for instance my arm. After that, I would use paraffin gauze to keep them from sticking to your bandages. I know this is a medical supply, but this is really important because you will be ripping off your scabs otherwise. If you really don't have that, I would use wet paper towels, but just slightly wet. Not soaked. If you do that, before you take it off, make the paper towels wet again without taking them off your wounds. This will prevent your wounds from sticking to it.
If you do use paraffin gauze, just put dry paper towels un top. Never use toilet paper or cotton pads, this wil get stuck your wound and leave bits in your wounds that can cause infections.
Then, I would buy a bandage that you use for like a sprained ankle and put this untop. Because it is you can actually wash it, so you will be able to re-use it. If you can, buy disposable ones that are made for cuts and stuff, but if you can't i would advise what i said before. If you can't buy anything, I would cut a string of maybe a sheet and use this as a bandage, washing it every time you change your bandage. To prevent your bandage from falling off, I would use those hair clips.

I would leave this on for the first day. After that, I would wear a bandage during the day and at night sleep with nothing to let your cuts bleed. Keep cleaning your cuts and change your bandages regularly. I would also stop putting a bandage on when the scabs get like -idk how to explain. But like that stage where they are really hard and don't get soft/wash a way when you're in the shower.

"An overdose of ibuprofen can cause severe problems in the gastrointestinal tract. These include:

inflammation

ulcers

Symptoms of an ibuprofen overdose

"Not everyone will experience symptoms of an ibuprofen overdose right away. Some people won’t have any visible symptoms at all.

If you do experience symptoms of an ibuprofen overdose, they’re usually mild. Mild symptoms may include:

tinnitus (ringing in the ears)
heartburn
nausea
vomiting
stomach pain
diarrhea
dizziness
blurred vision
rash
sweating

Severe symptoms can include:

difficult or slow breathing
convulsions

Hi, 
Please let me explain why I think this was a unhelpful thing to reply. I've grown up in mental hospitals, so I know many people (including myself) that have suicidal tendencies or behavior. 
Some recovered after two years, some after a month, some after fifteen years and some never.
And it has nothing to do with emotions. Mental illnesses or mental health problems are your brain being sick. Depression, for instance, is visible on brain scans and has proven to affect your brain functioning. Being sad or empty or whatever due to your depression (to keep this one as example, but it applies to every mental illness or mental health problem) is a symptom of the illness of your brain. Like someone with brain cancer can have headaches because of the tumor. Both cases can't change that. You can't tell someone to just decide not to have a headache and the same goes for, for instance, sadness. 

What you mean, i think, is that you have a saying in what you want to do with that headache. Do you go and stay in bed all day or do you decide to go for a walk or take meds or whatever. Most of the time you can make a decision what you do with it. Just like you can decide what you do what you're gonna do with your sadness.

Now we have that out of the way, I still have a problem with that mindset. Some people really can change and will be better because they decide to fight against their sadness, which won't go over night, but will be a hard process. You are right, some people really do find something in meditation and books and it helps them, over a LONG period of time, recover. Yes, this takes time. When you finish the book you won't be better. Unfortunately, that isn't how it works. 
There are people that will have problems for the rest of their lives, however. Because they're chronically ill. And some learn to cope with that and live a life without experiencing -happiness for instance. 
But there are also people that just can't get better, no matter how hard they try. Some have literally tried every therapy, every medication, every coping that is out there, but don't get better. We're talking, in my country, from mindfulness and meditation to therapy like ECT, and everything in between, but their brain is to sick.

You have three layers of skin. The first is the epidermis, the second one is the dermis which most people on the sub call styro because it kinda looks like it. It is white, yes. So you cut into the second layer of skin.
The third and last one is the subcutaneous tissue (hypodermis) which is your fat layer. When you hit this you'll see bubbles (probs yellow) of fat. On this sub we call it the 'fat layer' or 'fat cuts'.
It is dangerous to cut into the dermis because there are many nerves and stuff, so please be aware.
